title: Fender Splash Shield Removal and Installation — SVT Performance Package
introduction:
For the Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, removing the wheel exposes the splash shield and its separate groups of push-pin retainers. I treat those groups like the teeth of a zipper: release every attachment before asking the panel to move. The illustrations identify the retainers in magenta and the shield in blue.

The procedure below covers shield removal and refitting, with the required wheel-removal, lifting and wheel-installation preparation included. The wheel and tire remain assembled.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the vehicle safely parked, the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Complete remote-start disabling first, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If the menu needs ignition ON, keep a valid key inside and the engine OFF: from ignition OFF, release the pedals and press the start button once; if already ON, leave it ON rather than pressing again.

For an automatic, establish engine-off ignition ON in the same way if it is not already ON, then hold the service brake and select Neutral in the ground-level cabin. With the parking brake and chocks maintaining restraint, release the brake pedal and press the button once to switch ignition OFF. For a manual, switch ignition OFF if it is ON, then select Neutral with the engine OFF while maintaining those restraints. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before hands-on service. Keep the parking brake applied throughout the job.

The ignition controls follow the Ford Mustang owner manual; service precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Personal protection and material handling
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp edges. Failure to use the applicable protection may cause serious personal injury. Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified lubricant; improper chemical handling may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Hoist setup
items.detail: Keep the parking brake applied and restrain wheels remaining on the ground while positioning the vehicle for lifting. With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist rated for its weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the lifting points by the triangles stamped into the uni-body sheet metal or frame, along the sill areas near the front and rear wheel openings. Position the lift arms at those points as shown in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631), section 100-02. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury; incorrect hoist positioning can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Protect the underbody
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage components. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, where fitted, and avoid damaging the axle or rear cover. Check underbody clearance before driving onto a drive-on lift. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper; the covers will be damaged.

items.name: Jack precautions
items.detail: The vehicle's emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire and must not be used to raise the vehicle for this repair. If a service jack is used during preparation, verify its capacity for the loaded or modified vehicle, use a hard, level surface and the specified lifting points, set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Support the raised vehicle with floor stands before going underneath; a jack can lower unexpectedly. Failure to secure and support the vehicle can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Wheel removal precautions
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so may cause serious personal injury. Do not use heat to loosen a seized wheel nut because it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Do not weld or peen a damaged wheel: install a new wheel if it needs those repairs, since wheel failure can cause serious personal injury. See [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Brake dust precaution
items.detail: Do not breathe friction dust or blow it from brake components with compressed air. Use approved dust-control techniques and avoid dispersing residue; it can present serious respiratory and other health hazards. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). Control dust before disturbing dusty components or beginning mounting-face preparation.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

items.name: Clean the mounting faces
items.detail: Apply the dust controls above first; these are separate from the following mating-face preparation. Before reinstalling the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its mounting face and the mating hub, brake-disc or brake-drum face. Secure any rotor-to-hub fasteners so they cannot interfere with those faces. Contamination or interference can let the wheel nuts loosen and the wheel come off in motion, causing loss of control, serious injury or death. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

items.name: Lubricate only the pilot interface
items.detail: Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft® High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant / XL-2 only between the wheel's central pilot bore and the hub pilot that locates it. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc/drum mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces; contact there may damage components.

items.name: Install and tighten the wheel
items.detail: Position the wheel and install the wheel nuts finger tight initially. Keep the parking brake applied while lowering, and restore the ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground. With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the nuts in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads. The supporting drawing crosses from the top nut to the lower-left, then upper-right, upper-left and lower-right. Skipping the cross pattern can produce excessive brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

items.name: Required follow-up
items.detail: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; failing to retighten may cause serious injury to occupants.

items.name: Restore the grounded parked state
items.detail: After tightening, with the vehicle fully grounded, chocked and the parking brake still applied, restore its parked gear. For an automatic, enter the ground-level cabin with the valid key, release the pedals and press the button once from known ignition OFF for engine-off ON. Hold the service brake, select Park, then release the brake and press the button once for OFF. For a manual, keep the engine and ignition OFF and select a parked gear. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before leaving.

edits.text: NOTE: The LH (left-hand) side is shown; removal and installation on the RH (right-hand) side are similar.
edits.why: Use the illustrated attachment layout as the guide for the opposite side without treating the pictured view as that side.

edits.text: Remove the wheel and tire assembly. Refer to: Wheel and Tire (204-04A Wheels and Tires, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The wheel blocks access to the shield's wheel-arch attachments. Following the lifting preparation above, remove the wheel nuts and take off the assembled wheel and tire. The linked [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) also supplies the mounting-face preparation and final tightening requirements needed when the wheel goes back on.

edits.text: Remove the magenta retainers around the louvered end of the shield, including those beside the rectangular opening and along the outer and lower edges. Raise each center pin away from the panel to release the retainer, then withdraw its body.
edits.why: The inset shows a separate center pin sitting proud of the retainer body. Releasing that pin lets the body come out; pulling on the shield while the retainers are locked loads its attachment holes instead.

edits.text: Remove the next group of magenta retainers shown across the wheel-arch section and its lower attachment edges. Release each center pin, then withdraw the retainer body.
edits.why: These attachments extend across the broad arch section. I check this whole group before moving on so a quiet little fastener does not become an accidental panel anchor.

edits.text: Remove the remaining magenta retainers shown from underneath, including the attachments beside the brace and around the other louvered end and lower flange. Release each center pin, then withdraw the retainer body.
edits.why: The underside view exposes attachments that are less obvious from inside the wheel opening. Completing this group releases the remaining illustrated fastening points.

edits.text: With the illustrated retainers removed, lower the fender splash shield out of the wheel opening in the direction shown.
edits.why: The blue highlight identifies the complete shield, and the downward arrow shows its removal movement. The surrounding gray body and suspension parts remain in place.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: raise the splash shield into position, align its attachment holes and reinstall the retainer groups in reverse order. With each center pin raised, seat the retainer body in its hole, then press the pin down to lock it. Reinstall the wheel and tire assembly using the referenced wheel-installation requirements.
edits.why: Seating the retainer bodies before locking their center pins restores the illustrated attachment arrangement. Finish the wheel installation with clean mating faces, correctly restricted pilot lubricant, the specified tightening pattern and torque, and the required later retightening.
